Come nourish your mind, body, and spirit.

✦
The refuge

The back room. East Sixth Street, five minutes from Tompkins Square Park.

Caravan of Dreams has fed the East Village since 1991.

Its name echoes a Sufi teaching. The mystic Bahaudin Naqshband described humanity as a dream-caravan: individuals traveling together, yet each suspended in their own subjective reality, carried by their own hopes and illusions.

This week, we hope to gather those dreams together, right here in NYC.

As you enter the space, you’ll discover a bohemian restaurant with a small stage and a kitchen that runs all day: warm coffee, healthy snacks, exquisite plates, and drinks with or without alcohol. Behind it, the private back room has a screen and A/V, for the conversations that want a door closed.

The doors are open from 11 AM to 11 PM, all week, for the curious locals and the weary travelers alike.

✦
The curation

During Climate Week, we want to curate a space of convergence to cross-pollinate regenerators, where both native New Yorkers and outsiders can come to nourish their minds, bodies, and spirits.

Together, we hope to nurture the conditions for patrons to exchange ways of future-proofing our neighborhoods and communities by tapping into resilience practices and structures.

We are partnering with Caravan of Dreams to make this project happen, and will leave this place better than we found it by ensuring they make at least $3,000 a day in food sales.

We exclude nobody at the door. We shape the week by curating its hosts, and every event clears the same short list:

  • It cross-pollinates. It mixes worlds that do not usually share a room: stewards and builders, capital and justice, artists and organizers, locals and visitors.
  • It builds capacity. Guests leave holding one thing they can do in their own neighborhood, and three ways to take a next step: support it, celebrate it, amplify it.
  • It starts from what already exists. The neighborhoods around us already practice resilience. Events amplify that work rather than arriving as though nothing is here.
  • Hosts stay in the room. Plan to spend time in the space beyond your own slot, and end on something people can act on locally.
  • Nothing is for sale. No product demos, no deal flow, and no case study so specific that nobody else can use it.
